Get processed tag archival data

Source: R/get_archival_data.R
get_archival_data.Rd

Fetches processed archival data from tags. The data downloaded from csv files hosted on lifewatch.com and then read into R. Providing at least one of the following arguments is required: tag_serial_number, animal_id, or animal_project_code.

Usage

get_archival_data(
  tag_serial_number = NULL,
  animal_id = NULL,
  animal_project_code = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  limit = FALSE,
  progress = TRUE,
  return_as = c("tibble", "arrow")
)

Arguments

tag_serial_number

Character (vector). One or more tag serial numbers.

animal_id

Integer (vector). One or more animal identifiers.

animal_project_code

Character (vector). One or more animal project codes. Case-insensitive. An animal project can contain many gigabytes of archival data. Downloading this data may take a while and exceed the available RAM or Storage of your computer.

path

Character. A path to an existing directory where the csv files will be stored. If NULL, the csv files will be stored in a temporary directory that is deleted when R is restarted.

limit

Logical. Limit the number of returned records to 100 (useful for testing purposes). Defaults to FALSE.

progress

Logical. Show a progress bar while fetching data. Defaults to TRUE.

return_as

Character. One of "tibble" or "arrow". Whether to return the data as an in memory tibble or an out of memory arrow dataset. The latter is recommended for large datasets, but requires more disk space and may be slower to query. When selecting "arrow" keep in mind that the downloaded data will remain stored on your computer until R is restarted.

Value

Depending on the value of return_as, either an arrow::Dataset or a data.frame with the archival data values. The resulting table has the following columns:

  • tag_id: The tag id of the tag that recorded the data.

  • timestamp_utc: The timestamp of the measurement in UTC.

  • measurement_type: The type of measurement (e.g. "Temp", "Pressure, etc.).

  • measurement_value: The value of the measurement.

  • measurement_unit: The unit of the measurement (e.g. "C", "Pa", etc.).

  • animal_project_code: The animal project code of the animal that recorded the data.

  • animal_id: The animal id of the animal the tag was attached to.

  • tag_serial_number: The tag serial number of the tag that recorded the data.

Returning large amounts of data out of memory

If you are fetching a large amount of data, it is recommended to use return_as = "arrow" to return an out of memory object. This will allow you to query the data without loading it all into memory at once. Keep in mind that the downloaded data will remain stored on your computer until R is restarted. If you want to keep the data, you can provide a path to an existing directory where the csv files will be stored via the path argument. See arrow::Dataset for more information.

Temporary storage of csv files

When return_as is set to arrow, the downloaded csv fils will be stored in tempdir() even when no path has been provided. This is neccesairy because of the way arrow dataasetquery objects work; they need to be able to access the csv files on disk. To remove these files from your computer, you can either restart R or manually delete the files from the temporary directory.

See also

Other access functions: get_acoustic_deployment_logs(), get_acoustic_deployments(), get_acoustic_detections(), get_acoustic_projects(), get_acoustic_receivers(), get_animal_projects(), get_animals(), get_bibliography(), get_cpod_projects(), get_package(), get_tags()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive() & etn:::credentials_are_set()
  get_archival_data(tag_serial_number = "A15757", limit = TRUE)
}
